info.title: Campbooks API
info.description: The Campbooks HTTP API. Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`. Operations require an OAuth 2.1 bearer token with the scope they list (401 without a valid token, 403 without the scope) unless they are public. Those operations are rate-limited per caller (a person per app, an app on its own) in classes: reads, writes, and mail sends (`x-campbooks.rate_limit: send`, counted per person across their apps). Over a limit they answer 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`, in seconds. The `/bff/*` operations serve the web app only: they authenticate with its session cookie instead of a token.

post.summary: Ask Scout, and get its answer as it is written.
post.description:
The same request as `assistant.ask_chat`, answered as Server-Sent
Events once every check passed (a refusal is an ordinary problem
answer). Events, each `data` a JSON object: `thinking` (`{"delta"}`:
Scout's reasoning as it arrives, at most 8,000 characters in all),
`step` (`{"tool"}`: a tool starting), `text` (`{"delta"}`: the answer's
words as they arrive; words before a `step` are not part of the answer),
then exactly one of `done` (the stored Scout message, as `ask_chat`
answers it) or `error` (a problem: `chat_failed` or
`ai_daily_limit_reached`). A comment every 10 seconds keeps the
connection open. The question is stored when the stream opens; a
stream that ends before `done` leaves Scout's message stored as
`failed`, with no text.

get.summary: Follow a workspace's changes.
get.description:
A Server-Sent Events stream of what changed in the workspace, for clients
that keep a cache: each `change` frame names a record and an operation
(`{"cursor","record":{"type","id"},"op":"upsert"|"delete","version"}`),
never its contents; refetch what you show. Frames: `ready` (where the
stream starts), `change`, `heartbeat` (every heartbeat interval from the
open, busy or idle), `reset` (your token is unknown or expired, or
something you cached went out of sight: refetch everything, continue
from the token given), `revoked` (you no longer belong to the
workspace) and `closing` (the stream ends; reconnect with your token).
`ready`, `change`, `heartbeat` and `reset` carry a resume token as
`cursor` and as the SSE `id`, so `EventSource` resumes on its own. A
token is opaque, new on every frame and good only for the caller it was
given to: keep the latest, never parse or compare one. You only receive changes of records a read operation you
hold a scope for returns, and nothing in the stream (tokens, heartbeats,
resets) depends on changes you may not see.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last resume token received; resumes after it.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The last resume token received (any frame's `cursor`), for clients
that cannot send `Last-Event-ID` (the header wins when both are
present). Omit it to start from now.

post.summary: Scout's reply for an intent, or your draft rewritten, as it is written.
post.description:
The same request as `conversations.write_reply`, answered as a
Server-Sent Events stream once every check passed (a refusal is an
ordinary problem answer). Events, each `data` a JSON object:
`thinking` (`{"delta"}`: Scout's reasoning as it arrives, when the model
shows it, at most 8,000 characters in all), `text` (`{"delta"}`: the
reply's words as they arrive, at most 4,000 characters), then exactly one
of `done` (a `ReplyText`: the whole reply, as `write_reply` answers it)
or `error` (a problem: `reply_failed` or `reply_timed_out`), after which
the stream ends. A comment every 10 seconds keeps the connection open.
The stream ends with `reply_timed_out` after 30 seconds without a sign
from the model or 2 minutes in all. Nothing is saved or sent, and an
`Idempotency-Key` does not make the answer replayable.

bearer.description:
An OAuth 2.1 access token (a JWT) issued by this instance's identity provider, the issuer configured as `CAMPBOOKS_AUTH__ISSUER`. Each operation lists the scope it requires; operations with an empty requirement are public. Scopes:

- `admin:access`: Reach the instance administration API, if your account has an admin profile. Granted to Campbooks' own apps only.
- `assistant:read`: See what you told Scout about how it should act.
- `assistant:write`: Tell Scout how it should act, and turn your sentences into rules to check.
- `attention:read`: See what needs you: the items on your Home.
- `attention:write`: Put items on your Home off until later, and bring them back.
- `connectors:read`: See the outside accounts connected to your workspaces and how their sync is doing.
- `connectors:write`: Connect outside accounts (such as Gmail), sync them now and disconnect them.
- `conversations:read`: Read your inboxes, conversations and messages.
- `conversations:send`: Write drafts and send messages, replies and forwards from your inboxes.
- `conversations:write`: Mark conversations read or unread, star, archive, label and move them between streams.
- `identity:clients`: Register, rotate and remove a workspace's own apps and their secrets.
- `identity:read`: See your account, its ways in and the mailboxes waiting to be connected.
- `identity:write`: Change your account and connect or discard the mailboxes waiting on it.
- `pages:read`: See the pages you may open, and who they are shared with.
- `pages:write`: Make, edit, move, share and delete pages, and add files to them.
- `schedule:read`: See your calendars and events, your calendar settings, and when you are free.
- `schedule:write`: Create, change, delete and answer events, add them to your provider calendars, and change your calendars and calendar settings.
- `search:read`: Search the records you may read (conversations need conversations:read too).
- `system:read`: Read operational status, and report the app's own errors and timings.
- `tasks:read`: See your tasks and the ones you handed to someone.
- `tasks:write`: Add tasks, change them, mark them done and hand them to a teammate.
- `workspaces:admin`: Manage workspaces you own or administer: settings, members, invitations, deletion and the security log.
- `workspaces:read`: See your workspaces and who belongs to them.
- `workspaces:write`: Create workspaces, accept invitations and leave workspaces.

session.name: __Host-campbooks_session
session.description: The web app's session cookie, set by `/bff/callback` (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`; named `campbooks_session` when the instance's public URL is plain http). Unsafe methods also need the `X-Campbooks-CSRF: 1` header and a same-origin request.

tags.name: workspaces
tags.description: Workspaces, members and roles, invitations and the security log. Workspace-owned resources live under `/api/v1/w/{workspace_id}/`; a caller who is not a member (or a client token bound to another workspace) gets 404.

tags.name: connectors
tags.description: Connections to outside accounts (Gmail, Zoho Mail): connect with the provider's consent, see their health, sync now, disconnect. Credentials are never returned.

tags.name: conversations
tags.description: Inboxes, conversations and messages on any channel (email first), sorted into streams. Workspace-owned: a user sees the inboxes they are a member of; a client token bound to the workspace sees them all.

tags.name: identity
tags.description: Accounts and their ways in, and this instance's OAuth 2.1 authorization server: discovery, keys, authorization, tokens, revocation, sign-in with a provider, and the mailboxes a sign-up granted, waiting for a workspace. The protocol endpoints (`/.well-known/*`, `/oauth2/*`, `/auth/*`) serve browsers and OAuth clients; they answer 404 while another identity provider serves the instance.

tags.name: attention
tags.description: What needs you: one queue per member of what the records you may open ask of you (conversations today), with Later per member.

tags.name: search
tags.description: One search over the records you may open: conversations today. Words in English, Portuguese, Spanish and French with accents ignored, Gmail-style operators, highlights as plain-text segments. Results come only from the containers (inboxes) you may see, checked at query time.

tags.name: assistant
tags.description: What you told Scout about how to act, and turning a sentence you type into rules to check. Compiling uses the `complete` AI role only when you ask, and sends it your sentence and your own addresses and label names, never your mail; nothing is saved until you save a rule through the conversations module.

tags.name: schedule
tags.description: Your calendars and their events: the provider calendars you connect and your own Campbooks calendar, where Scout puts the dated things it reads in your email. Events have a kind; free time is answered from your working hours.

tags.name: tasks
tags.description: What you have to do: your tasks, with a due date, a plan (a day, or Later), a hand-off to one teammate and an undo for every change. Personal: a task is seen by who it is with, and by who handed it off.

tags.name: pages
tags.description: What you and your team write: pages in a tree, each a block document that several people edit at once and the server merges, with mentions of people, threads, tasks and events, backlinks, files, sharing by member and role, and a trash that keeps what you delete for 30 days. Off unless the instance turns it on (`CAMPBOOKS_PAGES__ENABLED`); while off, every operation answers 404.

tags.name: changes
tags.description: The change feed: a Server-Sent Events stream per workspace of the records that changed (ids only), so clients refetch only what they show.

tags.name: bff
tags.description: The web app's backend-for-frontend: sign-in, the session cookie and same-origin API access. Browsers only; other clients call `/api/*` with their own OAuth token.
